note: Research batch 8 (human clinical trials depth) for ChatGPT to plug into data.js. Every PMID verified against the NCBI E-utilities API (titles and years match). Each study tagged with plant (oilIds), terpenes (compoundIds), uses (categories). Merge rule: skip any study whose pubmedId already exists in data.js.

studies.title: Peppermint oil (Mintoil) in the treatment of irritable bowel syndrome: a prospective double blind placebo-controlled randomized trial.
studies.authors: Cappello G, Spezzaferro M, Grossi L, Manzoli L, et al.
studies.finding: Four weeks of enteric-coated peppermint oil significantly reduced IBS symptom scores versus placebo, with 75% versus 38% of patients achieving greater than 50% symptom reduction.
studies.limitations: n=57; patients with small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, lactose intolerance, or celiac disease were excluded, limiting generalizability.

studies.title: The efficacy of 5% topical tea tree oil gel in mild to moderate acne vulgaris: a randomized, double-blind placebo-controlled study.
studies.authors: Enshaieh S, Jooya A, Siadat AH, Iraji F
studies.finding: Topical 5% tea tree oil gel was 3.55 times more effective than placebo on total lesion count and 5.75 times more effective on the acne severity index, with similar tolerability.
studies.limitations: Short trial duration; no head-to-head comparison against standard acne therapies such as benzoyl peroxide.

studies.title: Rosemary oil vs minoxidil 2% for the treatment of androgenetic alopecia: a randomized comparative trial.
studies.authors: Panahi Y, Taghizadeh M, Marzony ET, Sahebkar A
studies.finding: After 6 months, both rosemary oil and minoxidil 2% significantly increased hair count with no significant difference between groups, while scalp itching was more frequent with minoxidil.
studies.limitations: No placebo arm; 6-month duration only, so long-term efficacy and safety are unknown.

studies.title: A multi-center, double-blind, randomised study of the Lavender oil preparation Silexan in comparison to Lorazepam for generalized anxiety disorder.
studies.finding: Oral lavender oil capsules (Silexan) reduced Hamilton Anxiety scores comparably to lorazepam over 6 weeks (45% versus 46% reduction) without sedation or abuse potential.
studies.limitations: No placebo arm; 6-week treatment period only.

studies.title: Therapy for acute nonpurulent rhinosinusitis with cineole: results of a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
studies.authors: Kehrl W, Sonnemann U, Dethlefsen U
studies.finding: Oral cineole significantly reduced acute rhinosinusitis symptom scores versus placebo after both 4 and 7 days of treatment.
studies.limitations: Tested isolated cineole capsules, not eucalyptus oil; acute nonpurulent cases only.

studies.title: A randomized, controlled trial of tea tree topical preparations versus a standard topical regimen for the clearance of MRSA colonization.
studies.authors: Dryden MS, Dailly S, Crouch M
studies.finding: MIXED RESULT: mupirocin cleared nasal MRSA carriage significantly better than tea tree cream (78% versus 47%), but tea tree preparations outperformed chlorhexidine and silver sulfadiazine at clearing skin sites and lesions.
studies.limitations: Hospital patients only; 5-day regimen; tea tree was inferior to the standard for nasal decolonization.

studies.title: Healing advantages of lavender essential oil during episiotomy recovery: a clinical trial.
studies.authors: Vakilian K, Atarha M, Bekhradi R, Chaman R
studies.finding: Lavender oil sitz baths significantly reduced wound redness compared with povidone-iodine during episiotomy recovery, with no difference in pain scores or complications.

studies.title: Effect of aromatherapy massage on menopausal symptoms: a randomized placebo-controlled clinical trial.
studies.authors: Darsareh F, Taavoni S, Joolaee S, Haghani H
studies.finding: Aromatherapy massage significantly lowered Menopause Rating Scale scores versus both placebo massage and no treatment, while massage alone also beat no treatment.
studies.limitations: A multi-oil blend was tested, so individual oil effects were not isolated; single-center study.

studies.title: Lavender essential oil in the treatment of migraine headache: a placebo-controlled clinical trial.
studies.authors: Sasannejad P, Saeedi M, Shoeibi A, Gorji A, et al.
studies.finding: Inhaled lavender oil reduced migraine severity significantly more than placebo (3.6 versus 1.6 VAS points), with 92 of 129 attacks responding entirely or partially.
studies.limitations: Acute attacks only; no comparison against standard migraine medications.

studies.title: The effects of clinical aromatherapy for anxiety and depression in the high risk postpartum woman - a pilot study.
studies.finding: Clinical aromatherapy with rose oil produced significantly greater improvements than control on both anxiety (GAD-7) and depression (EPDS) scales in high-risk postpartum women, with no adverse effects.
studies.limitations: Small pilot study; not blinded; larger trials recommended.

studies.title: The Effectiveness of Aromatherapy for Depressive Symptoms: A Systematic Review.
studies.authors: Sanchez-Vidana DI, Ngai SP, He W, Chow JK, et al.
studies.finding: The systematic review concluded aromatherapy shows potential as a therapeutic option for depressive symptoms, with aromatherapy massage more beneficial than inhalation alone.
studies.limitations: Included studies varied in methodological quality; substantial heterogeneity across trials.

studies.title: Evaluation of massage with essential oils on childhood atopic eczema.
studies.authors: Anderson C, Lis-Balchin M, Kirk-Smith M
studies.finding: NULL RESULT: aromatherapy massage showed no significant advantage over massage alone for childhood atopic eczema, and the authors raised possible allergic contact dermatitis from the essential oils themselves.
studies.limitations: Only 8 children studied; mothers chose varying oil blends, so no single oil can be evaluated.

newOils.name: Rose
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from petals. Citronellol and geraniol rich; improved anxiety and depression scores in a postpartum pilot study.
newOils.safety: Generally well tolerated; very expensive — expect adulteration in cheap oils.
